preamble: Common Turkic z regularly corresponds to Oghur (Chuvash) r, as in Turkish yüz '100' beside Chuvash śĕr. The direction of this change is disputed. Under the zetacism hypothesis, Proto-Turkic had a second rhotic, r₂, which Common Turkic turned into z while Oghur kept it as r. Some scholars reconstruct this r₂ as palatalized *ŕ [rʲ], and the Wikipedia Proto-Turkic article lists it in parentheses as a disputed phoneme. Under the rival rhotacism hypothesis, which Róna-Tas and others prefer, Proto-Turkic had *z, Common Turkic kept it, and Oghur changed it to r. If the rhotacism view is right, this cell does not apply. Wiktionary now writes the sound as rᶻ, which leaves its phonetic value open.
sources: Stachowski, M. (2014). Remarks on the investigation of the oldest layer of Turkic loan-words in Hungarian. Studia Etymologica Cracoviensia 19, 215-222. https://doi.org/10.4467/20843836SE.14.015.1658
